mainTopic: How many loaves different מנחות need, and whether changing that number makes them invalid; then the start of a new משנה on how much grain is sifted for the עומר, שתי הלחם, and לחם הפנים.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining שמואל's ruling that לחמי תודה baked as only four loaves are valid. He follows a ברייתא that lets most מנחות have more or fewer loaves than usual. רב הונא rules that a מנחת מאפה baked as one loaf is valid, because the פסוק spells מצת as if it were singular. רב פפא challenges him from שמואל's ruling, and the גמרא answers that the two simply disagree. A new משנה then lists how much grain is used to make the flour for the עומר, שתי הלחם, and לחם הפנים. The גמרא explains these amounts by whether the grain is barley or wheat, and new or old. A ברייתא adds that the flour amount must be exact, but the amount of grain may change. Next comes a משנה about how many sifters were used for each offering, where רבי שמעון says the flour is just sifted until it is clean. A ברייתא then teaches that for לחם הפנים alone, the flour or even raw wheat may be bought, because התורה חסה על ממונן של ישראל. The פרק ends, and the new פרק opens with a משנה on how much flour the loaves of a תודה use.

steps.title: שמואל follows a ברייתא that allows changing the number of loaves
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's ruling, that לחמי תודה baked as four loaves are valid, follows the תנא קמא of a ברייתא. That תנא says most מנחות stay valid even if the number of loaves is changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like this תנא, as it is taught in a ברייתא: All מנחות where one made more loaves or fewer loaves than required are valid, except לחם הפנים and the חביתין of the כהן גדול. Some say: also the לחמי תודה and the loaves of a נזיר must have the right number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where שמואל's ruling comes from. He follows a ברייתא that says changing the number of loaves usually does not make a מנחה invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says only two מנחות must have the exact number of loaves: לחם הפנים and חביתי כהן גדול. The יש אומרים adds לחמי תודה and the loaves of a נזיר. שמואל's ruling only works with the תנא קמא, since by the יש אומרים four loaves for a תודה would be invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offerings (plural of מִנְחָה)
Their loaves; here it means the set number of loaves
The shewbread: twelve loaves placed on the שולחן each שבת
The daily griddle-cake מנחה of the כהן גדול
The loaves brought with a קרבן תודה (thanks offering)
Some say: a second opinion in the ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up the main question of the sugya: is the number of loaves essential, and for which מנחות?

phrases.english: He holds like this tanna,
phrases.notes: "He" is שמואל, whose ruling about four loaves for the תודה came just before this.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:
All the meal offerings where one increased the number of their loaves,
or where one decreased the number of their loaves, are valid,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִלֶּחֶם הַפָּנִים וַחֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: except for the shewbread and the High Priest's griddle-cakes,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה וּנְזִירוּת.
phrases.english: And some say: also the loaves of the thanks offering and of naziriteship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion earlier by giving the source for שמואל's ruling about לחמי תודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a source: the ruling follows one side of a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought four loaves for a תודה should be invalid, since the set number is ten of each kind.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows the תנא קמא, who allows changing the number of loaves for every מנחה except לחם הפנים and חביתי כהן גדול.

steps.title: רב הונא: an oven-baked offering made as one loaf is valid
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a מנחת מאפה baked as a single loaf is valid. His reason is that the פסוק spells the word מצת, which can be read as one loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: A מנחת מאפה that one baked as one loaf has fulfilled the obligation. What is the reason? "מצת" is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new ruling: one loaf is enough for a מנחת מאפה. He bases it on how the word is spelled in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא 2:4) writes the word for unleavened loaves without a ו, so it can be read מצת, a single loaf. From that spelling רב הונא learns that even one loaf is valid, even though normally ten are made.

keyTerms.meaning: An oven-baked meal offering
One loaf
He has fulfilled his obligation; the offering is valid
What is the reason?
Read as singular: one unleavened loaf

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא's proof is about spelling, not meaning. The word is normally understood as "loaves," but because it is written without a ו it can be read as "loaf."

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
An oven-baked meal offering that one baked
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean "that he baked."

phrases.english: as one loaf has fulfilled the obligation.
What is the reason?
"Matzat" (a loaf) is written.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:4. It's spelled without a ו, so it can be read as one loaf. Some versions also have the round-bracket word מצות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's general rule to a specific ruling, with a פסוק source, about one מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחת מאפה baked as one loaf is valid, because the פסוק writes מצת in a form that can be read as singular.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges רב הונא's spelling proof
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out that רב הונא's reasoning means a plural spelling would require many loaves. But שמואל allowed just four loaves for a תודה, even though that פסוק is spelled מצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: The reason is that "מצת" is written; but if "מצות" were written, it would not be valid? Yet regarding the לחמי תודה, "מצות" is written, and רב טובי בר קיסנא said in שמואל's name: לחמי תודה baked as four loaves are valid!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רב הונא's logic. He brings a case where the plural spelling is used and yet fewer loaves are still allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the singular spelling is what makes one loaf valid, then a plural spelling should mean you need many loaves. But by תודה the פסוק (ויקרא 7:12) says מצות, plural, and שמואל still allows only one loaf of each kind. So רב הונא's reasoning seems to clash with שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges it: a strong objection
But if it were written ... it would not be? An inference from the opposite case
But look: introduces a contradicting source
Unleavened loaves, plural spelling with a ו
Four loaves, one for each of the four kinds of תודה bread

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to this:
The reason is that "matzat" is written,
but if "matzot" were written, it would not be valid?
But regarding the thanks offering loaves, where "matzot" is written,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Tovi bar Kisna said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה שֶׁאֲפָאָן אַרְבַּע חַלּוֹת – יָצָא!
phrases.english: Thanks offering loaves that one baked as four loaves are valid!
phrases.notes: The תודה normally has forty loaves, ten of each of four kinds, so four means just one of each kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of רב הונא in step 2, using שמואל's ruling from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the singular spelling מצת is why one loaf is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reasoning suggests a plural spelling needs many loaves. Yet שמואל allows fewer loaves by תודה, where the spelling is plural.

steps.title: Answer: שמואל's ruling disagrees with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל's ruling and רב הונא's view are simply two different opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: That statement disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא in two words: שמואל and רב הונא do not hold the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds the number of loaves matters unless the פסוק hints otherwise, so by תודה (spelled מצות) four loaves would be invalid. שמואל follows the תנא קמא of the ברייתא, who allows changing the number. So there is no contradiction, just a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees: the two statements are separate opinions

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: one loaf is valid for a מנחת מאפה because of the singular spelling מצת. שמואל: four loaves are valid for a תודה, following the תנא קמא. The גמרא says these two views disagree.

phrases.english: That statement disagrees.
phrases.notes: "That statement" is שמואל's ruling about the four loaves; it disagrees with רב הונא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two opinions that argue: the contradicting source follows a different view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא assumed שמואל and רב הונא must agree, so שמואל's ruling disproves רב הונא's reasoning.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל argues with רב הונא, so his ruling is no proof against רב הונא's reading.

steps.title: New משנה: how much grain is sifted for each offering
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה gives the amounts: the עומר is one עשרון of flour from three סאין of grain, שתי הלחם is two עשרונים from three סאין, and לחם הפנים is twenty-four עשרונים from twenty-four סאין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The עומר would come as one עשרון from three סאין. שתי הלחם came as two עשרונים from three סאין. לחם הפנים came as twenty-four עשרונים from twenty-four סאין.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists how much grain was used to produce the flour for three communal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each offering uses a set amount of very fine flour, sifted out of a larger amount of grain. The ratio is different: the עומר takes three סאין for one עשרון, שתי הלחם takes three סאין for two עשרונים, and לחם הפנים takes one סאה for each עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה
The barley offering brought on the sixteenth of ניסן
One tenth of an איפה, a set measure of flour
A larger dry measure; three סאין make one איפה
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two measures: the עשרון is the flour that is actually used, and the סאין are the raw grain it was sifted from.

phrases.english: Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: הָעוֹמֶר הָיָה בָּא עִשָּׂרוֹן מִשָּׁלֹשׁ סְאִין,
phrases.english: The omer would come as one tenth of an ephah from three se'a,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם שְׁתֵּי עֶשְׂרוֹנִים מִשָּׁלֹשׁ סְאִין,
phrases.english: the two loaves as two tenths from three se'a,
the shewbread as twenty-four tenths
from twenty-four se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָעוֹמֶר הָיָה בָּא עִשָּׂרוֹן מִשָּׁלֹשׁ סְאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic, not connected to the loaf-number discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עומר: one עשרון from three סאין. שתי הלחם: two עשרונים from three סאין. לחם הפנים: twenty-four עשרונים from twenty-four סאין.

steps.title: Why the עומר needs three סאין for one עשרון
steps.stepSummary: The עומר needs three סאין of grain for one עשרון of flour because it is new barley, which has a lot of waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Since it comes from the new crop and from barley, a choice tenth of flour can only come from three סאין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the עומר needs so much grain, three סאין, to make only one עשרון of flour. It answers that new barley is poor quality, so it must be sifted a lot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things make the grain weak: it is fresh from this year's crop, and it is barley, not wheat. The flour must be מובחר, the best quality. So you need a large amount of grain and sift away most of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain from the new, fresh crop of this year
Barley, a coarser grain than wheat
A tenth of an איפה of top-quality, well-sifted flour
A larger dry measure of grain; plural סאין

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking why the עומר in the משנה needs three סאין of grain to give just one עשרון.

phrases.english: Since it comes from the new crop,
and it comes from barley,
a choice tenth does not come
except from three se'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first amount listed in the משנה of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the עומר needs three סאין for one עשרון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: New barley has a lot of waste, so much grain is needed to get one choice עשרון.

steps.title: Why שתי הלחם get two עשרונים from three סאין
steps.stepSummary: שתי הלחם gets twice as much flour from the same three סאין because it is made from wheat, which is cleaner than barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two loaves are two tenths from three סאין. Since they come from wheat, even though they come from the new crop, two tenths come from three סאין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שתי הלחם gets two עשרונים from three סאין, while the עומר got only one. The difference is that שתי הלחם is wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שתי הלחם is also new grain, just like the עומר. But wheat is better than barley, so the same three סאין give double the good flour.

keyTerms.meaning: Wheat, a better-quality grain than barley
Even though

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם שְׁתֵּי עֶשְׂרוֹנוֹת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ סְאִין –
phrases.english: The two loaves: two tenths from three se'a –
since they come from wheat,
even though they come from the new crop,
two tenths come from three se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּמֵחִיטִּין אָתְיָין, אַף עַל גַּב דְּמֵחָדָשׁ אָתְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same reasoning as step 6 and shows how wheat changes the result.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wheat is cleaner than barley, so even new wheat gives two עשרונים from three סאין.

steps.title: Why לחם הפנים gets one עשרון from each סאה
steps.stepSummary: לחם הפנים gets one עשרון from every סאה because it is old wheat, which is the cleanest grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The showbread is twenty-four tenths from twenty-four סאין. What is the reason? Since it comes from wheat and from the old crop, a choice tenth comes from one סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third amount in the משנה. לחם הפנים needs only one סאה for each עשרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both factors are good. It is wheat, not barley, and it is old grain, not new. So very little is sifted away, and one סאה is enough for one choice עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain from an older crop, which is drier and cleaner

steps.whatToRemember: Two things set the amount: wheat or barley, and new or old. New barley (עומר) needs the most grain. New wheat (שתי הלחם) needs less. Old wheat (לחם הפנים) needs the least.

phrases.english: The showbread: twenty-four tenths
from twenty-four se'a –
What is the reason?
Since they come from wheat,
and they come from the old crop,
a choice tenth comes from one se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה עֶשְׂרוֹנוֹת מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה סְאִין – מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the three amounts of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why לחם הפנים needs only one סאה for each עשרון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Old wheat is very clean, so one סאה gives one choice עשרון.

steps.title: Changing the flour measure disqualifies, changing the grain measure does not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the עשרון of flour is too big or too small, the מנחה is פסולה. If only the number of סאין of grain was changed, it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: any מנחות where one made the עשרון measure bigger or smaller are disqualified. If one made the measure of their סאין bigger or smaller, they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells us how strict these numbers are. The amount of flour must be exact, but the amount of grain it came from does not have to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עשרון is the actual size of the קרבן, so changing it makes the מנחה פסולה. The number of סאין is only the best way to get good flour. So if someone used more or fewer סאין, the מנחה is still כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure, the size of the amount used
Made it more / made it less
Disqualified, not valid as a קרבן
Valid, fit to be brought

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two measures. The עשרון is the flour itself and must be exact. The סאין are the grain you start with, and changing them does not ruin the מנחה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the numbers of סאין in the משנה are the ideal way to do it, not a requirement that makes the קרבן valid or not.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
All the meal offerings where one increased the measure of their tenth,
or where one decreased the measure of the tenth –
are disqualified.
If he increased the measure of their se'a,
or decreased the measure of their se'a –
they are valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל הַמְּנָחוֹת שֶׁרִיבָּה בְּמִדַּת עֶשְׂרוֹנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the numbers of סאין, the גמרא teaches that these numbers are not critical, while the עשרון is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Changing the עשרון of flour makes a מנחה פסולה. Changing the number of סאין of grain leaves it כשרה.

steps.title: The משנה: How many sifters for each offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the עומר was sifted 13 times, שתי הלחם 12 times, and לחם הפנים 11 times.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The flour of the עומר was sifted with thirteen sifters, שתי הלחם with twelve, and לחם הפנים with eleven.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה tells us how many sifters were used to clean the flour for each of the three grain offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the earlier steps. The עומר is new barley with the most waste, so it needs the most sifting. שתי הלחם is wheat and needs less. לחם הפנים is old wheat, the cleanest, so it needs the least.

keyTerms.meaning: Sifted
A sifter or sieve
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread placed on the שולחן in the מקדש

phrases.english: MISHNA: The omer was sifted
with thirteen sifters;
the two loaves with twelve;
and the showbread with eleven.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָעוֹמֶר הָיָה מְנוּפֶּה בִּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה נָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה continues the topic of preparing flour for these three offerings, now about sifting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עומר: 13 sifters; שתי הלחם: 12; לחם הפנים: 11.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: No fixed number, just fully sifted
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says there was no set number of sifters. The flour simply had to be sifted until it was completely clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: There was no fixed number. Rather, he would bring fine flour sifted as much as it needed, as it says 'And you shall take fine flour and bake it,' meaning it must be sifted completely.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues with the first opinion in the משנה. He says the count does not matter, only the result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives exact numbers. רבי שמעון says the goal is fully sifted flour, however many rounds that takes. He supports this from the word סֹלֶת, fine flour, in the פסוק about לחם הפנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed amount or set number
Fine flour
As much as it needs; completely

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
They had no fixed number;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא סוֹלֶת מְנוּפָּה כָּל צׇרְכָּהּ הָיָה מֵבִיא,
phrases.english: rather, he would bring fine flour sifted as much as it needed,
as it is said: “And you shall take fine flour and bake it,”
until it is sifted as much as it needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיָה לָהֶן קִצְבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the fixed numbers given in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no set number of sifters. The flour must be sifted until it is completely clean.

steps.title: How the sifting worked: fine, coarse, fine, coarse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the flour went back and forth between fine and coarse sifters.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: תנו רבנן: With a fine sifter, then a coarse one; again a fine one, then a coarse one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא describing the method of sifting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fine sifter let the tiny dust fall through and kept the flour. A coarse sifter let the flour through and kept the bran. Switching back and forth cleaned the flour from both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine sifter with small holes
A coarse sifter with large holes

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
With a fine one, with a coarse one;
with a fine one, with a coarse one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the many siftings in the משנה were actually done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sifting alternated between fine and coarse sifters.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: Thirteen sifters stacked up
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר describes thirteen sifters in the מקדש, stacked one above the other. The top one caught bran and the bottom one caught fine flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: There were thirteen sifters in the מקדש, one above the other. The top one caught bran, and the bottom one caught fine flour.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא describes what the sifting setup in the מקדש looked like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He describes thirteen sifters in the מקדש, arranged one above the other. The top sifter caught the bran, and clean fine flour collected in the bottom one.

keyTerms.meaning: Bran, the husk part of the grain
Catches or collects
The top one / the bottom one

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
There were thirteen sifters in the Temple,

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ וְזוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ,
phrases.english: this one above that one, and this one above that one;
the top one catches bran,
the bottom one catches fine flour.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה נָפוֹת הָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different description of the sifting setup from the one in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thirteen stacked sifters: bran caught at the top, fine flour at the bottom.

steps.title: The verse teaches that ready fine flour may be bought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns back to רבי שמעון's פסוק and brings a ברייתא: the words 'fine flour and bake it' teach that for לחם הפנים, one may buy flour that is already sifted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי שמעון says there was no fixed number. The Rabbis taught: 'Fine flour and bake it' teaches that fine flour may be bought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's line from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that learns more from his פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק רבי שמעון used is now read to say that for לחם הפנים, the flour may be taken already sifted. It does not have to be ground and sifted from scratch for this purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Is taken or bought

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיָה לָהֶן קִצְבָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: They had no fixed number.
The Rabbis taught:
“Fine flour and bake it” —
teaches that fine flour may be bought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי שמעון's opinion and the פסוק from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For לחם הפנים, one may buy flour that is already fine flour.

steps.title: What about buying wheat kernels?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that even unground wheat kernels may be bought for לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that even wheat kernels may be bought?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up its next point by asking for a source that even raw wheat may be bought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that ready flour may be bought. Now the question goes further: may one buy plain wheat and grind it later?

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
Wheat kernels

phrases.english: And from where do we know that even wheat kernels may be bought?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 14 from bought flour to bought wheat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that wheat kernels, not only flour, may be bought for לחם הפנים.

steps.title: 'And you shall take' means in any form
steps.stepSummary: The word וְלָקַחְתָּ teaches that the grain may be taken in any form, even as wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'And you shall take' — in any way.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from the extra word 'and you shall take.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'take' is general, so it includes taking the grain as plain wheat kernels too.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse comes to teach
In any case; in any form

phrases.english: The verse says: “And you shall take” —
in any form.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: וְלָקַחְתָּ teaches that the grain may be taken in any form, including wheat kernels.

steps.title: Does this apply to other מנחות too?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that perhaps other מנחות may also be bought as wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is the same for other מנחות?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible wider reading so it can limit it in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'take' was read broadly, one might think every מנחה may be bought as wheat. This 'I might have thought' is set up only to be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: I might have thought
The other grain offerings

phrases.english: I might think that it is so even for other meal offerings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the rule from step 16 reaches beyond לחם הפנים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether other מנחות may also be bought as wheat kernels.

steps.title: 'It' limits the rule to לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: The word אֹתָהּ limits the rule to לחם הפנים alone, because of the saving involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'it' — only this one, because of the saving.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by limiting the rule to לחם הפנים using the word 'it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: אֹתָהּ points to this specific offering, so other מנחות are left out. The reason given is חִיסָּחוֹן, a saving that applies to לחם הפנים in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: It; this one specifically
Sparing; saving

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה argues about the number of siftings: fixed numbers, or רבי שמעון's 'as much as needed.' For לחם הפנים alone, the flour may be bought ready, or even as wheat kernels.

phrases.english: The verse says: “it,”
because of the sparing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by limiting the rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אֹתָהּ limits buying as wheat to לחם הפנים alone, because of the saving.

steps.title: What does 'because of the saving' mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks what the ברייתא meant when it said לחם הפנים may be bought as wheat 'because of the saving.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What does 'because of the saving' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר picks up the last words of the ברייתא from the previous step and asks what they mean. He is setting up his own explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said only לחם הפנים may be bought as wheat, and gave the reason 'מפני החיסחון.' That reason is short and unclear: whose saving, and why does it matter? רבי אלעזר wants to spell it out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean
Because of
Saving, sparing (of money or loss)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
What is the meaning of "because of the sparing"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the reason given at the end of step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the ברייתא's phrase 'מפני החיסחון' means.

steps.title: The Torah protects Jewish money
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people, so it lets them save by buying wheat instead of expensive sifted flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The Torah spared the money of the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers his own question: the 'saving' means the Torah does not want the Jewish people to lose money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לחם הפנים needed a lot of flour every week, and buying it already sifted costs much more. By allowing the purchase as plain wheat, the Torah saves public money. This turns a short phrase into a general principle: the Torah cares about people's property.

keyTerms.meaning: Had pity on, spared
The money of the Jewish people

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea 'התורה חסה על ממונן של ישראל' is a well-known principle that appears in other places in ש״ס too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: The Torah spared the money of the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Saving' means the Torah protects the money of the Jewish people, so cheaper wheat may be bought.

steps.title: Where is this idea hinted in the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the Torah we see a hint that the Torah cares about Jewish money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is it hinted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the פסוקים for רבי אלעזר's principle. It is setting up the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר stated a big idea about how the Torah thinks. The גמרא wants to see that this idea is hinted somewhere in the Torah itself, not just a reasonable guess.

keyTerms.meaning: Where
Is it hinted
A hint (a source that suggests an idea without saying it outright)

phrases.english: Where is the allusion to this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the principle stated in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that hints that the Torah protects Jewish property.

steps.title: Water from the rock was given to the animals too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק about water from the rock: 'you shall give drink to the congregation and to their animals,' showing that ה׳ cared even about their livestock.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall give drink to the congregation and to their animals.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק: when ה׳ made water come out of the rock, He made sure the animals drank too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A miracle was done not only to save people but also to save their animals, which were their property. If ה׳ cares about their animals, that shows the Torah cares about their money. This is the hint for רבי אלעזר's principle.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall give drink
Congregation
Their animals, their livestock

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lets לחם הפנים be bought as wheat because 'התורה חסה על ממונן של ישראל,' and the hint is that the water from the rock was also for the animals.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"So you shall give drink to the congregation and to their cattle."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The miracle of water from the rock included the animals, showing ה׳ cares about Jewish property.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אלו מנחות נקמצות
steps.stepSummary: The פרק called אלו מנחות נקמצות ends here.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, אלו מנחות נקמצות.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is a closing formula, not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'הדרן עלך' mean 'we will return to you,' showing a wish to come back and learn this פרק again. A new פרק starts right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
From which a fistful (קמיצה) is taken

phrases.english: We will return to you, "These meal offerings have a handful removed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק אלו מנחות נקמצות.

steps.title: How much flour the loaves of a תודה use
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that the loaves of a קרבן תודה used five Jerusalem סאין, equal to six wilderness סאין, which is two איפות, or twenty עשרונים: ten for חמץ loaves and ten for מצה loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The תודה would come from five Jerusalem סאין, which are six wilderness סאין. That is two איפות, each איפה being three סאין, which equals twenty עשרונים: ten for the חמץ and ten for the מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה giving the amount of flour used for the loaves brought with a קרבן תודה, and how it is split between חמץ and מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה translates the measure into several units: the Jerusalem סאה is bigger, so five of them equal six of the older wilderness סאין. Six wilderness סאין make two איפות, and since an עשרון is a tenth of an איפה, that is twenty עשרונים. Half goes to the חמץ loaves and half to the מצה loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks offering, which comes with loaves of bread
A measure of volume
A measure equal to three (wilderness) סאין
A tenth of an איפה
Leavened bread
Unleavened bread

steps.confusionAlert: There are two sizes of סאה here. The 'Jerusalem' סאה is bigger than the 'wilderness' סאה, so five of one equal six of the other. It is the same amount of flour, just counted in different units.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The thanks offering would come
phrases.notes: He means the loaves that come with the תודה, not the animal itself.

phrases.english: from five Jerusalem se'a,
which are six wilderness se'a.
That is two ephahs,
each ephah being three se'a,
which equals twenty tenths:
ten for the leavened loaves and ten for the matza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק התודה after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves of a תודה use twenty עשרונים of flour (five Jerusalem סאין, six wilderness סאין, two איפות), ten for חמץ and ten for מצה.
